# Jubilees Chapter 31 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob visits Isaac; Isaac's blessings of Levi and Judah

---

**31:1** Jacob came to his father Isaac and his mother Rebekah at Mamre — the valley of Hebron — in the second year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

**31:2** Jacob kept Rachel and Leah and his handmaids and all his sons and his daughter and all his livestock and herds with him, and dwelt at his father's house at Mamre.

**31:3** On the new moon of the seventh month, Isaac his father held a feast and sent for Jacob his son, who came and brought a gift to his father.

**31:4** Jacob was afraid to come before his father, for his father was old and his eyes were dim. But his mother Rebekah said to him: "Do not be afraid; go in to him."

**31:5** Jacob came in to his father Isaac. Isaac stretched out his hands and embraced him and wept over his neck and kissed him on the face, saying: "My son, I am old and my eyes are dim and I cannot see you, but I can smell your fragrance and hear your voice."

**31:6** Jacob said to his father: "I am Jacob your son, who loves you as a son ought to love his father."

**31:7** Isaac said: "Why have you come, my son?" Jacob said: "I came to see you, to kiss your hands and your face, to receive your blessing, and to ask that you pray for me."

**31:8** Isaac held his son Jacob and embraced and kissed him and wept greatly.

**31:9** Isaac called his son Levi and said: "Come near to me." Levi came near, and Isaac placed his right hand on his head and his left hand on his shoulder.

**31:10** He said: "May the God of all, the Lord of all ages, bless you and your sons throughout all the generations of the ages. And may the LORD your God make you and your seed a priestly people to him — the most holy of all peoples — for all ages.

**31:11** May he give to you and your seed and to your descendants' descendants all the greatness of the priesthood that can be given. May you be holy and great before God, and may your seed be exalted and accepted before him.

**31:12** May you be a minister of God's sanctuary, blessed and sanctified. Be a prince among the sons of God; may all peoples be subject to you, and may your sons and the sons of your sons be holy.

**31:13** He has chosen you from among all flesh to serve him and to minister before him in his sanctuary — to be his minister and a blessing in the midst of all the earth."

**31:14** He let Levi depart and called Judah near, placing his right hand on his head, and said:

**31:15** "May the LORD God of all bless you forever, my son. May he give you power and greatness for victory over all the nations of the earth. May all peoples who do not know you fear your name, and all the kings of the earth stand in dread before you.

**31:16** May your fruit be abundant and your seed be made great. May your rule be great in the earth. Be exalted, my son, and strengthen the power of your seed.

**31:17** Be a king and a prince among all peoples, and may all nations bow before you."

**31:18** He placed both hands on his head and kissed him, saying: "May the LORD God bless you — the holy God of Israel who rules over all the earth. May he sanctify you and choose you as a holy people."

**31:19** Jacob rejoiced and blessed and praised God, and fell on his face before his father Isaac and bowed down.

**31:20** Then the spirit of prophecy descended upon Isaac's mouth and he said: "Blessed are you, O LORD God of Israel, who have kept me and all the generations of my fathers — those who did not transgress your covenant and your ordinances. You have blessed Jacob and blessed Levi and Judah."

**31:21** He arose and wept when he saw Jacob's twelve sons standing before him. He was glad, and blessed them all.

**31:22** Jacob departed from before his father Isaac that day glad and rejoicing, and brought the good news to his mother Rebekah.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering following LOGOS. Isaac's dual blessings of Levi (priestly vocation, vv.10-13) and Judah (royal vocation, vv.15-17) are programmatic for Jubilees' two-office theology. The "spirit of prophecy" formula (v.20) was rendered consistently across all translators. PNEUMA's emotional warmth in the reunion scene (vv.5-8) informed some phrasing choices.*
